text:
Alice: Quick sync: span naming & attributes for model routing + cache hits. Want to land a convention we can use across runtime, router, and console dashboards.
Ben: +1. Our current traces are a mess - sometimes spans are "inference", sometimes "model_exec", and dashboards can't group them.
Carla: Proposal: span name = "llm.request" and use attributes to encode phase: "phase": "router|dispatch|exec|cache|postproc". Thoughts?
Dmitri: I like a stable noun like llm.request. But worried about high-cardinality attributes (model_version/model_size). We should keep keys curated.
Elaine: We definitely need model.* attrs: model.name, model.variant, model.quantization. Also tokens.in/tokens.out, and cache.hit boolean.
Frank: Agreed, but model.variant can explode. Suggest model.family and model.revision; family=flan-t5-xxl, revision=v1_q4_0
Ben: For routing analytics we need routing.policy and routing.reason (e.g., "latency_sla", "cost_opt", "capacity_fallback"). These are low-cardinality.
Alice: Also need route.destination (hosted|dedicated|private) and route.pool (e.g., gpu-pool-a). But pool might be sensitive - maybe redaction or hashing?
Carla: Can we keep route.pool but only surface hashed_pool in telemetry to avoid leaking infra details? hash id + mapping stored elsewhere.
Dmitri: Important: do NOT include user prompt or any PII in span attributes. We should have prompt.redacted = true and prompt.digest for traceability if needed.
Elaine: For tokens: use tokens.prompt and tokens.generated, both ints. Also add cost.estimate_usd as float; helpful for per-token cost dashboards.
Frank: Cache attributes: cache.hit (bool), cache.tier (prefix|kv|global), cache.latency_ms. For cache hits we should make a small span named "llm.cache" nested under request.
Ben: Sampling/export: we should mark spans with telemetry.sample_reason (e.g., "error", "audit", "random_0.01"). Important for exporters to keep errors always.
Alice: Retention policy: traces older than 90d aggregated to metrics. Raw traces kept 30d for most customers, 180d for enterprise. We need span.attribute: retention.tier.
Carla: How about naming conventions for console charts? Use metric labels that map directly: model.name -> model, routing.policy -> route_policy, cache.hit -> cache_hit
Dmitri: One more: link traces to billing by adding billing.tenant_id (hashed) and billing.usage_unit = "token" or "request". Keep tenant id hashed.
Elaine: Quick suggestion for final attribute list snippet:
```
span.name: "llm.request"
attributes:
  model.name, model.family, model.revision, model.quantization
  tokens.prompt, tokens.generated, cost.estimate_usd
  cache.hit, cache.tier, cache.latency_ms
  routing.policy, routing.reason, route.destination
  telemetry.sample_reason, retention.tier, billing.tenant_hash
```
Frank: LGTM. Also add span.kind = "server" and status for errors: error=true + error.message(short)
Ben: Implementation note: runtime should attach these attrs at dispatch and exec; router attaches routing.*; cache layer emits its own llm.cache span.
Alice: Ok let's write this up and land a spec doc + proto. @Ben can you create a short PR with the attribute names and types? @Carla can you add the console mapping?
Ben: On it. I'll open PR in infra/telemetry with examples and exporter mapping.
Carla: I'll add dashboard mappings and a migration note.
devops-bot: Reminder: deploy window tonight 23:00-00:30 UTC. :rocket:
Alice: Thanks all, follow-up PRs due EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
